Dr. Elaine Eshbaugh, Dementia Simulation House Founder and Professor of Gerontology at the University of Northern Iowa, explores the critical link between anxiety and cognition in individuals living with dementia. Through actionable strategies to minimize anxiety, she reveals how creating calming environments fosters better communication, social engagement, and quality of life for those living with dementia. 

Dr. Elaine Eshbaugh is a professor of Gerontology and Family Studies at the University of Northern Iowa and has coordinated the Gerontology program since 2007. She earned her MS and PhD from Iowa State University. In 2022, she founded and now directs UNI’s Dementia Simulation House. Dr. Eshbaugh frequently speaks on dementia and leads trainings to promote dementia-friendly communities. In this inspiring TEDx talk, Melodie Leung reveals how trust, in yourself and in others, is the true catalyst for extraordinary creativity.
As an architect who began her career at 25 under the mentorship of the legendary Zaha Hadid, Melodie shares how being sent into boardrooms in New York, Hong Kong, and Germany long before she felt ready taught her a profound lesson: creative leadership isn't about having all the answers — it's about being fully dedicated to the journey.
Through vivid stories, from building a cardboard city with friends as a teenager in suburban Chicago, to learning musicality at the piano, to leading the construction of a landmark sculptural billboard in London. Melodie reveals the two sides every creative must learn to bridge:
The technical and the emotional – Precision without feeling is incomplete. Feeling without the ability to deliver is ineffective. True creative impact lives where both meet.

title: Cultivating Creative Leadership | Melodie Leung | TEDxWoodLaneWomen

description: Katelyn explores how academic success is a marathon, and sleep is your ability to run. Sleep is a repetitive and mundane topic, at least to students. We're often told to get enough sleep due to health benefits, but how many of us listen? How many of us acknowledge the role of sleep in study and work? How many of us aren't ignorant and blind to the accumulating effects of a lack of sleep? It's an old tale, yet apathetic attitudes remain stagnant during all this time. You need sleep to run, to succeed. It's time to change our mindset on this seemingly simple issue and better ourselves for our health. Sleep is the fuel that helps us excel on the track. Truc Anh (Katelyn) is a Year 11 student from British Vietnamese International School, HCMC, who was inspired to examine how sufficient sleep leads to achievement. Por meio de um projeto autoral, ela amplia o ciclo de vida dessas criações, transformando fantasias em novos objetos e levando-as para outros carnavais na Europa. Sua proposta conecta cultura, sustentabilidade e responsabilidade com o planeta.

Em seu talk, Mariana nos convida a repensar o tempo das coisas: se uma fantasia nasce de tanta história e trabalho, por que deveria durar tão pouco? Ao estender sua vida útil, ela transforma desperdício em legado — e o Carnaval em potência sustentável.
On the TEDxRio stage, Mariana reveals that Carnival costumes go far beyond the 90 minutes on the avenue. Each piece carries art history, cultural references, and lived experiences that should not end in a single night.

Como primeiro bailarino do Teatro Municipal, ele revela como transita entre dois universos aparentemente distintos: o palco clássico e a avenida. seu talk, ele mostra que a criação nasce da observação atenta e das conexões — entre corpos, histórias, sons e símbolos. Durante muito tempo, enfrentou a dificuldade de ser vista além do Carnaval — de provar que também poderia ser executiva, líder e tomadora de decisões. Em vez de limitar sua trajetória, a experiência como passista se tornou sua força. Ela ajudou a desmontar o estereótipo da “mulher objeto” e transformá-lo em uma narrativa de autonomia e presença.

Em seu talk, Rafaela mostra que ser passista não é sobre espetáculo, mas sobre confiança, protagonismo e voz. E, de forma simbólica, convida toda mulher a experimentar, em algum momento da vida, o que é ser passista: ocupar seu espaço, mover-se com intenção e reconhecer-se como potência, nunca como ornamento.

author: TEDx Talks
description:
No palco do TEDxRio, Felipe, historiador, conduz o público por uma viagem às origens do Carnaval. Ele explica como a festa nasce na Europa, no período que antecede a Quaresma, quando por alguns dias as hierarquias eram suspensas e as pessoas podiam ser quem gostariam de ser.

Ao chegar ao Brasil, essas tradições se encontram com as culturas africanas da diáspora e se transformam profundamente. Ritmos, saberes e formas de celebrar reinventam o Carnaval, tornando-o uma expressão genuinamente brasileira — marcada por resistência, mistura cultural e potência criativa.
On the TEDxRio stage, Felipe, a historian, takes the audience on a journey through the origins of Carnival. He explains how the celebration began in Europe, in the period leading up to Lent, when for a few days social hierarchies were suspended and people could become who they longed to be.

When these traditions arrived in Brazil, they encountered the cultures of the African diaspora and were profoundly transformed. Rhythms
title: O MISTÉRIO DO CARNAVAL | Felipe Ferreira | TEDxRio Salon

Sua fala mergulha nas origens do samba, mostrando que essa expressão nasce da resistência, da ancestralidade e da vivência coletiva. O samba surge da rua, do encontro, da necessidade de transformar dor em ritmo e cotidiano em celebração. A rua, como ele nos lembra, é a primeira escola: é ali que se aprende observando, escutando, repetindo, respeitando os mais velhos e entendendo que cada verso carrega uma história.

On the stage of TEDxRio, Marquinhos takes us on a journey that goes far beyond music. He speaks about what it truly means to be a sambista — not as a profession, but as identity, belonging, and cultural responsibility.

In this deeply moving TEDx talk, Marina Davidova confronts the silent epidemic hiding behind startup culture — loneliness.
With 16 years in venture capital and experience backing over 150 companies, Marina reveals what most founders won't say out loud: 76% feel lonely, and the rest are too busy pretending they're not. Behind the pitch decks and polished confidence lies a world of masks — performed for investors, customers, and teams — where real human connection quietly disappears.
Through her own raw story of betrayal, immigration, and rebuilding during COVID, Marina shares how losing trust in partnerships, friendships, and herself led her to a powerful realisation: control is an illusion, but we do have agency over the inputs that shape our lives.
She introduces her Triple B framework , a personal operating system for resilience:
1. Body – Scheduled recovery, movement, and letting the body carry pain away.
2. Brain – Feeding the mind through learning, curiosity, and growth.

Drawing on nearly 30 years in the beauty industry, from manufacturing floors to brand development, Dee introduces her Three A's framework, a simple but transformative approach to taking back control of what you put on your skin:
1. Assess over assume – Stop buying on impulse and start understanding what your skin actually needs. 2. Align over follow – Look beyond the trending hero ingredients and find brands that truly share your values,  from sustainability to what's hiding in the 85–95% of a formulation nobody talks about. 3. Action over overwhelm – Use the tools now available to us, including AI, to cut through the marketing noise and make choices that fit your needs, your values, and your budget

His creative journey weaves together diverse disciplines, ranging from visual storytelling and large-scale installations to product design and branding, anchored in his core belief that discarded materials hold the power to be reborn as objects of meaning, beauty, and cultural relevance.
